subject: Holdback structure in Exhibit C — earnout & payment holdback language
messages:
From: Jane Alvarez <jane.alvarez@novahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novalegal Team <legal@novalegal.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit C draft — holdback mechanics

Connor —

Thanks for the updated order form. Procurement ran the numbers and we have two questions before we can circulate to internal finance: 1) the 10% holdback in Exhibit C releases on a 90-day basis but the milestone language references "adoption targets" that aren't numerically defined; can we tie the holdback to concrete run-rate thresholds or usage bands instead of the current qualitative language? 2) the earnout/true-up section in section 3.2 looks like a unilateral recovery right; our legal team flagged it as an effective clawback that could trigger escrow demands.

Attached is a short markup from our side (we call it a holdback worksheet) that proposes staggered releases (30%/30%/40%) with defined usage buckets. Happy to walk through on a call — is Thursday morning possible?

Best,
Jane Alvarez
Sourcing Manager — NovaHealth
procurement@novahealth.com
Attachment: NovaHoldback_Worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Alvarez <jane.alvarez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Novalegal Team <legal@novalegal.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit C draft — holdback mechanics

Jane —

Thanks, appreciate the worksheet. Thursday morning works for me (9:30 PT). I copied Lauren (legal) and Marissa (AM) so we can take notes and propose clean language beforehand. A few quick framing points so we use the call time well:

- The holdback is meant as a limited payment deferral tied to go-live and initial integration milestones (not a product-quality clawback).
- We are open to defining numeric usage bands; our concern is setting thresholds that are overly rigid and which could create perverse incentives for customer-side measurement.
- The earnout/true-up in 3.2 is intended to reconcile overbilled credits tied to forecast shortfalls — not to create a retroactive charge for ordinary usage. If NovaHealth prefers escrow mechanics we can discuss a capped escrow (e.g., 10% of first 12 months' committed spend with quarterly releases).

I'll circulate a proposed redline to Exhibit C (clean and markup) by EOD. Agenda for block: confirm release percentages, define usage buckets, and agree on audit/measurement rights.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
Attachment: Exhibit-C_redline_v2.docx (redline stub)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jane Alvarez <jane.alvarez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Novalegal Team <legal@novalegal.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Exhibit C draft — holdback mechanics

Connor/Jane —

Following our call, I've uploaded a tracked redline (Exhibit-C_redline_v3.docx). High-level legal positions we maintained:

1) Holdback vs. Escrow: We can accept a time-phased escrow release but prefer the language to reference "release upon attainment of defined usage bands or mutually-acknowledged onboarding milestones." We added explicit examples for measurement windows (30/90/180 days) so neither party is left with unbounded discretion.

2) Earnout / True-up: Reworded 3.2 to make it a reconciliation (credit or debit) limited to misapplied credits, invoicing errors, or manifest measurement errors — not retrospective service charges. Added a 60-day dispute window and a hard cap (10% of invoiced amount for the period) on recoveries.

3) Audit and Measurement: If NovaHealth requests an audit, we propose a single independent auditor with scope limited to billing and usage logs for the affected period. Cost allocation: losing party pays auditor costs unless the audit shows >10% error.

4) Termination Impact: If contract terminates for convenience within first 12 months, release schedule accelerates pro rata; if for cause, holdback may be retained only if we can show material breach tied to the holdback metric.

I've flagged a few optional alternate phrasings for the release percentages — we can present the default staggered release (30/30/40) or a straight 50/50 depending on their comfort.

Questions for Sales: are you comfortable with the 10% recovery cap? Does the team want to suggest a different escrow cap tied to committed spend tiers?

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Exhibit-C_redline_v3.docx (tracked changes), PaymentSchedule_v2.xlsx (stub)

From: Jane Alvarez <jane.alvarez@novahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novalegal Team <legal@novalegal.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit C draft — holdback mechanics

Lauren/Connor —

Thanks for the clear redline. A few initial responses from procurement/legal:

- The staggered release tied to 30/90/180 windows is acceptable provided the usage buckets are explicit. We'll propose numeric bands in our next markup (e.g., Band A: >= 75% of committed queries/mo; Band B: 50-74%; Band C: <50%).
- The 10% recovery cap is a good compromise; our finance team would like the cap to be expressed as "10% of verified invoiced spend for the first 12 months" (so we avoid a cap that grows unexpectedly).
- Audit language: we want the auditor to be mutually agreed (if we can't agree within 10 days, either party may nominate; the nominated auditor cannot be a competitor).

We'll return a counter markup by COB Monday with the numeric bands inserted and a sample calculation row in PaymentSchedule_v2.xlsx.

Jane
Attachment: NovaHoldback_Markup_v1.docx (redline stub), PaymentSchedule_v2.xlsx (annotated stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Alvarez <jane.alvarez@novahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novalegal Team <legal@novalegal.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit C draft — holdback mechanics

Jane —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed bands. We're aligned with the 10%-of-first-12-months phrasing (helps finance forecast). For practical next steps on our side:

1) I'll update the PaymentSchedule_v2.xlsx to include two scenarios (conservative and baseline) showing how the staggered release affects cashflow and true-up calculations across year 1.
2) Connor and I will plan a short internal run-through of the sample calculation Tuesday morning PT; Lauren, if you can confirm the dispute window & auditor-selection fallback language we'll include that in the clean markup.

We want to keep the overall commercial intact and avoid giving NovaHealth an ongoing clawback. If we land on the capped reconciliation + limited-scope audit + defined bands, we can sign off on pricing exhibit language.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0147
Attachment: PaymentSchedule_v2.xlsx (scenario stubs)
